h1: The 8 Best Headphones Under $100 for ANC and Calls, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 headphones under $100 scored on noise cancelling, call mics, comfort and battery, from Sony to budget picks.
summary: The Sony WH-CH720N is the best headphone under $100 for noise cancelling and comfort. The Soundcore Q20i gives the most battery with ANC, the JBL Tune 530BT is the call-friendly on-ear and the Rinsmola is the earbud choice. The BERIBES and a Bluetooth sleep mask round out the ladder.
intro: A $100 headphone budget does not mean you should spend $100. The mistake is treating the cap as a target: the best noise cancelling here is not the most expensive, and a set that lists in the $30 to $50 bracket can match a more costly rival on features. What you pay for above $50 is mostly polish, such as a better processor, a firmer hinge and more refined tuning, and few buyers use all of it.

We ranked eight picks from the listings on cancelling, call microphones, comfort, battery and price position. Five are Bluetooth headphones of the over-ear or on-ear type, two are true wireless earbuds, and one is a sleep mask with built-in speakers. Most sit well below the cap, and the Sony has no confirmed price bracket in our data, which we note in its entry.

Headphones in this range fail in predictable ways: ear pads that flake or compress, hinges that crack at the fold, batteries that drop sharply after a year, and noise cancelling that hums or thins out voices. Cancelling is also a spectrum: hybrid systems with four microphones handle steady noise like engines, but wind and voices slip through. We lean on stated specifications and say where a claim is a manufacturer figure.

products.name: Sony WH-CH720N Noise Cancelling Headphones
products.verdict: The lightest Sony noise cancelling headband, with adaptive sound and a processor you rarely see below a premium price.
products.description:
Sony's WH-CH720N is an over-ear wireless noise cancelling headset weighing just 192 grams, which Sony calls its lightest. It uses an Integrated Processor V1 with dual noise sensors, Adaptive Sound control and an adjustable Ambient Sound mode. The listing quotes up to 35 hours of battery life, with three minutes of charging giving up to an hour of playback, and beamforming microphones for calls. A USB Type-C cable is included.

It ranks first because it pairs active cancelling with a feather weight, so you can wear it for a full flight or workday. The V1 processor and DSEE sound engine give it a more refined voice and cleaner mids than the budget sets. It beats the Soundcore on comfort and call pickup, and trades away the Soundcore's longer 40 hour battery.

Buy it if you commute, fly or work in an open office and want the most comfortable ANC pair under $100. We could not confirm a live price bracket, so check the current price. The caveat is that 35 hours is shorter than rivals, and Sony's cancelling is good, not flagship-class.
pros: Quick charge saves a dead battery
products.idealFor: Frequent flyers and office workers who want a light, trusted ANC set.
products.skipIf: You need an IP rating or a hard-shell folding case.

products.name: Soundcore Q20i Hybrid ANC Headphones
products.verdict: Four-mic hybrid cancelling, 40 hours with ANC on, and a wired Hi-Res option.
products.description:
The Soundcore Q20i is an over-ear hybrid ANC headset with four built-in microphones, BassUp bass tuning and a quoted 40 hours of playback with ANC on. A five minute top-up is listed at four hours of playback, and it connects to two devices at once with automatic switching. The app adds EQ presets, HearID, spatial audio, ANC, Normal and Transparency modes, white noise and over-the-air updates.

It ranks second because it gives you near-Sony cancelling and a richer feature list at a lower bracket. The wired AUX cable unlocks Hi-Res certified audio, though the listing notes that noise cancelling does not work in AUX mode. It beats the JBL for cancelling, and loses to the Sony on weight and call clarity.

Buy it for remote work and commutes where you juggle a laptop and phone. It lists in the $30 to $50 bracket. The caveat is that ANC and a wired connection are mutually exclusive, so a long-haul flight with an in-flight jack means no cancelling.
pros: Hybrid ANC in the $30 to $50 bracket
cons: No ANC over the AUX cable
products.idealFor: Value hunters who want the strongest cancelling per dollar.

products.name: JBL Tune 530BT Wireless On-Ear Headphones
products.verdict: Pure Bass tuning, two beamforming mics per cup and a rated 76 hours.
products.description:
The JBL Tune 530BT is a foldable on-ear headphone with custom 33mm drivers tuned for Pure Bass sound, two beamforming mics on each earcup and a quoted 76 hours of battery. The listing says a five minute charge gives about five hours, a full charge takes about two hours, and the charging cable is not included. It supports multipoint pairing on Bluetooth 6.0, plus Fast Pair and Swift Pair for quick Android and Windows setup, and an app with Default, Bass and Vocal EQ presets.

It ranks third because call quality and battery are its strengths, but it has no active cancelling. It beats the earbuds for comfort over a long meeting, and loses to the Soundcore and Sony for noisy places. On-ear pads rest on the ear rather than around it, so some people find them tiring after two hours.

Buy it if you take lots of calls and want long battery for under $50. It lists in the $30 to $50 bracket. The caveat is that the box does not include a charging cable, so use one you already own.
cons: On-ear pads can tire the ear
products.idealFor: Call-heavy workers who want brand support and easy pairing.

products.name: Rinsmola G21Pro Wireless Earbuds
products.verdict: Compact earbuds with 14.2mm drivers, IP-X7 protection and a pocket-friendly 34 gram case.
products.description:
The Rinsmola G21Pro is a pair of true wireless earbuds with 14.2mm graphene drivers, Bluetooth 5.4, ENC call noise reduction and an IP-X7 water rating. Each bud weighs 3.6 grams and comes with three ear cap sizes, the pocket case weighs 34 grams, and a dual LED display shows charge levels. The listing quotes 6 to 8 hours per charge and about 40 more from the case.

It ranks fourth because earbuds sacrifice cancelling for portability, and the ENC here cleans up your voice on calls but does not quieten what you hear. It beats the BERIBES on pocketability and sweat resistance, and loses to the on-ear and over-ear picks for battery on one charge. Touch controls handle play, volume, track and calls.

Buy it for the gym, errands and light commuting. It lists under $30. The caveat is fit: a poor seal in the ear kills bass, so try each ear cap size.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants a cheap pocket pair.

products.name: BERIBES Bluetooth Over-Ear Headphones
products.verdict: A 0.38 pound folding over-ear rated over 120 hours, with Bluetooth 6.0.
products.description:
The BERIBES is a folding over-ear headset with dual 40mm dynamic drivers, six EQ modes, a 1000mAh battery rated for more than 120 hours and Bluetooth 6.0 with a listed range of about 33 feet. It weighs 0.38 pounds, uses memory-protein ear cushions, connects to two devices, and ships with a 3.5mm cable and a Type-C charging cable.

It ranks fifth because the battery and wired fallback are outstanding at the price, but it has no active cancelling and the listing names no warranty. It beats the Picun on EQ choice and Bluetooth generation, and loses to the JBL on call microphones, since it lists no beamforming mics.

Buy it if you want a long-life, light headset for desk work and travel. It lists under $30. The caveat is that, as with all headsets of this class, the pads and hinge are the weak points over time.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a spare pair.
products.skipIf: You need ANC or app support.

products.name: Picun B8 Wireless Bluetooth Headphones
products.verdict: A folding over-ear rated above 120 hours with dual 40mm drivers.
products.description:
The Picun B8 pairs dual 40mm drivers with a 1000mAh cell and a runtime above 120 hours, plus Bluetooth 5.3 and a listed 33 foot range. You get three EQ modes cycled by pressing the EQ button twice, touch controls, a built-in mic and cups that rotate 60 degrees on a folding frame wrapped in PU leather.

It ranks sixth because endurance is the headline and the tuning options are narrower than the BERIBES. It beats the earbuds in this guide on runtime between charges, but loses to every set above it on features. The listing warns owners to charge only from a 5V/1A or 5V/2A adapter and to avoid fast chargers, which is easy to forget when you travel.

Buy it if you are a student or traveler who hates charging. It lists under $30. The caveat is that PU leather can run warm and touch panels are fiddly with gloves.
products.idealFor: Students and travelers who hate charging.

products.name: Fhumsh A10 Bluetooth 6.0 Wireless Earbuds
products.verdict: Earhook earbuds with Bluetooth 6.0, an LED case display and an IPX7 case.
products.description:
The Fhumsh A10 is a Bluetooth 6.0 earbud set with 13mm drivers, ENC call noise reduction, reinforced earhooks and three sizes of gel tips. The listing quotes about 8 hours per charge with 50 hours in total, an IPX7 water-resistant case, and an LED display that shows the charge level of the case and each bud. The case weighs about 0.09 pounds.

It ranks seventh because the earhooks and the display make it a sound gym choice, but the claims are ambitious and the brand is unproven. It beats the sleep mask for general listening, and loses to the Rinsmola on published specifics such as weight per bud and driver size.

Buy it for workouts if you value secure hooks. It lists under $30. The caveat is that earhook designs do not suit everyone, and ENC only helps your callers.
pros: LED shows case and bud charge

products.name: LC-dolida Bamboo Cotton Bluetooth Sleep Mask
products.verdict: A 3D contour sleep mask with built-in Bluetooth 5.4 and a machine-washable bamboo-cotton cover.
products.description:
LC-dolida's sleep headphones combine a 3D contour bamboo-cotton blend mask with a built-in Bluetooth 5.4 module. The listing says the mask blocks light, wicks sweat, has an adjustable strap, and is machine washable. It lists in the $30 to $50 bracket, and it does not state driver size or battery runtime.

It ranks last because it is a sleep product first and a headphone second. It beats the earbuds for side sleepers, since there is nothing in your ear canal, but it loses to every headset on audio, mics and controls.

Buy it if you listen to podcasts or white noise as you fall asleep. The caveat is that runtime and drivers are unlisted, so treat it as a comfort item.
products.idealFor: Side sleepers and travelers who want audio in bed.

methodology.title: Noise control
methodology.description: Hybrid ANC, dual-sensor ANC, call-only ENC and plain passive isolation were separated, since only some sets quiet what you hear.

methodology.title: Call microphones
methodology.description: Mic counts, beamforming and wind claims were compared, because a good call mic matters more than a bass boost for most buyers.

methodology.title: Comfort and fit
methodology.description: Weight, pad style and ear tip options were weighed, with over-ear, on-ear and earbud types judged by how long you can wear them.

methodology.title: Battery and charging
methodology.description: Rated runtime, quick-charge figures and charging quirks were compared, noting where a number depends on ANC being off.

methodology.title: Price position
methodology.description: Most picks list under $50, and the Sony has no confirmed bracket, so we judged features against the $100 cap.

whatMatters.detail: Hybrid ANC uses microphones inside and outside the cup to cancel steady low noise such as engines and fans, while ENC only cleans your outgoing voice for callers. Budget ANC rarely handles voices or wind well, and it can add a faint hiss. Check whether the listing says active noise cancelling or just noise reduction, and count the mics, such as the four on the Soundcore.

Transparency or ambient mode pipes outside sound in so you can hear announcements, and adaptive controls change the cancelling to match your surroundings. They matter in daily use more than peak cancelling numbers. Look for named modes and an app on the listing.

Beamforming mics focus on your voice and reject the room, while a single omni mic picks up everything. For video calls, mic pickup matters as much as sound quality. Look for beamforming mentions and mic counts, and remember wired options may bypass the mic.

A quick-charge feature, such as three minutes for an hour of Sony playback or five minutes for four on the Soundcore, rescues a dead battery before a call. It matters more than a huge rated runtime for people who forget to charge. Check the listing for the minutes-to-hours figure and a USB-C port.

Over-ear cups spread pressure and seal well, on-ear pads rest on the ear and can tire it, and earbuds trade isolation for pocket size. Weight and clamp force decide whether you can wear them for hours. Check the weight in grams, the pad material and whether the cups swivel or fold.

cards.label: Over-ear
cards.text: Cups surround the ear for better isolation and comfort at long sessions, and better seal for bass. Picks: Sony WH-CH720N, Soundcore Q20i, BERIBES and Picun B8.

cards.label: On-ear
cards.text: Lighter and smaller, but pads press on the ear and can tire it. Pick: JBL Tune 530BT.

howToChoose.note: Choose over-ear if you wear them more than two hours at a time.

howToChoose.intro: What you spend the day doing decides the fit.

rows: LC-dolida Bamboo Cotton Bluetooth Sleep Mask

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Active noise cancelling, a quick-charge feature, a wired option for the in-flight system, and light weight. A folding hinge and a case help in a carry-on.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: Sony WH-CH720N for comfort and quick charge, and the Soundcore Q20i for the wired Hi-Res option, remembering its cancelling stops in AUX mode.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want industry-leading cancelling, premium build, better call mics and a longer software life. Those start beyond $100.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly listen at a desk. The Soundcore costs far less than the Sony, and the BERIBES costs even less.

faq.q: Is the Sony WH-CH720N really under $100?
faq.a: We could not confirm a live price bracket for it, so check the current price on Amazon before you buy. It is the only pick here without a stated bracket.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake at the $100 mark?
faq.a: Paying for a bigger driver or a bigger battery number when noise cancelling and call mics matter more. If you work in noise, spend on ANC and mics first, and do not pay extra for a 120 hour battery you will never drain.

faq.q: Is the Soundcore worth it over the JBL?
faq.a: If you need noise cancelling, yes, because the JBL has none. If you mostly take calls in a quiet room and want 76 hours of battery, the JBL's beamforming mics are the better fit.

faq.q: How do I connect the JBL to Windows or Android quickly?
faq.a: The listing mentions Fast Pair for Android and Swift Pair for Windows 10 and 11. Switch the headphones on, and your device should show a pairing prompt within seconds.

faq.q: Do I need to replace ear pads?
faq.a: Over a year or two, pads flake or compress, and replacement pads are only available for some models. Wipe pads with a dry cloth and avoid hot cars to extend their life.

faq.q: Can I use the sleep mask for regular listening?
faq.a: The LC-dolida is built for lying down, so it has no controls or drivers meant for general use. Treat it as a bedtime accessory, not a replacement for headphones.

finalTake: The Sony WH-CH720N is the best headphone under $100 for most people, thanks to light weight, solid ANC and call mics. The Soundcore Q20i is the value pick for ANC with 40 hours of battery, and the JBL Tune 530BT wins on calls without cancelling. Skip the sleep mask unless sleeping with sound is the whole point.
